{{Quote|Hold. However, as you can see, Guardian, we are not ordinary offworlders.''"<br />"''The Guardian is dead!''"<br />"''Yes, the old Guardian is dead. You are the Guardian now. It is you who protects the Emperor's mountain.|Grand Admiral Thrawn and Joruus C'baoth|<ref name="HttE" />}}
The '''Guardian of Mount Tantiss'''<ref name="HTTES">''[[Heir to the Empire Sourcebook]]''</ref> was a [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] assigned by [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] to guard his storehouse at [[Mount Tantiss/Legends|Mount Tantiss]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Wayland/Legends|Wayland]].<ref name="HttE" /> According to the [[Psadan]], the Guardian sought control over the natives of Wayland.<ref name="TLC">''[[The Last Command]]''</ref> Some years before [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]] [[Thrawn campaign|arrived]] on Wayland, the Guardian and the insane [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Cloning/Legends|clone]] [[Joruus C'baoth]] fought one another and the Guardian was killed. His body lay in a crypt in the [[Great palace (Wayland)|great palace]] surrounded by candles, one for every person who came to visit him after his death, all of whom (except Thrawn, [[Gilad Pellaeon/Legends|Gilad Pellaeon]], and [[Rukh/Legends|Rukh]]) were subsequently killed by C'baoth.<ref name="HttE" />

==Powers and abilities==
{{Quote|You seem certain, sir, that the Guardian will be a Dark Jedi.''"<br />"''“Who else would the Emperor have chosen to protect his personal storehouse?|Captain Pellaeon and Grand Admiral Thrawn|<ref name="HttE" />}}
[[File:Crypt-HttE1.jpg|left|thumb|265px|The crypt containing the body of the Guardian]]
The Guardian, as a dark Jedi, could wield [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], which he was believed to have used in service to Sidious to hunt down the Jedi. C'baoth fought the Guardian, which the insane clone interpreted as a noble Jedi act, fighting against the Imperial efforts to destroy the Jedi. This battle was the last time when C'baoth was required to exert himself until the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] clone was required to use [[Battle meditation/Legends|battle meditation]] to command fleets across star systems.<ref name="DFR">''[[Dark Force Rising]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|My original reasoning was just what's laid out here: that whomever Palpatine had left to guard his storehouse had been killed by Joruus C'baoth when he somehow stumbled on the place. To my mild surprise, speculation quickly arose that C'baoth was the original guardian, and it was merely because of his insanity that he thought he'd killed someone and taken his place. Such speculation is wrong, of course. I think&hellip;|[[Timothy Zahn]]|<ref name="20th">''[[Heir to the Empire: The 20th Anniversary Edition]]''</ref>}}
[[File:JoruusCbaoth-TLC5.jpg|right|thumb|270px|Joruus C'baoth killed the original Guardian and took his place]]
There was some debate over whether C'baoth was indeed the original Guardian, or if he in fact killed him. Although the inhabitants of Wayland remembered a battle between two powerful [[The Force/Legends|Force]] users, they were also all under the mental control of the insane [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]], whose account was only substantiated by the coffin within a crypt that Grand Admiral Thrawn and Captain Pellaeon were taken to. The pair ''assumed'' this crypt to hold the body of the original Guardian, but nothing substantiated this assumption other than the mad clone's statements.<ref name="HttE" /> The ''[[Dark Force Rising Sourcebook]]''<ref name="DFRS">''[[Dark Force Rising Sourcebook]]''</ref> and the [[Databank (original)|Databank]] also said that all evidence indicated that Joruus was the sole Guardian.<ref name="DB Joruus">{{DB|character|joruuscbaoth|C'baoth, Joruus}}</ref><ref name="DB Wayland">{{DB|location|wayland|Wayland}}</ref> However, none of these sources gave an entirely objective affirmation or denial. It was not until [[2008]], with the release of ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'', that it was confirmed within its entry on Mount Tantiss that the Guardian and C'baoth were separate entities.<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|II|337|Mount Tantiss}}</ref>
